name: CHOEP (Cyclophosphamide + DOXOrubicin + vinCRIStine + Etoposide + Prednisone)
histology: peripheral T-cell lymphoma (PTCL-NOS, AITL, and other nodal PTCL)

biomarkers.note: CHOEP is a cytotoxic five-drug backbone and is not biomarker-restricted for eligibility. CD30 is assessed on the diagnostic IHC/flow panel (Standard Guidelines (NCCN), T-cell Lymphomas v2.2026, lines 346, 352) and, when positive, supports adding brentuximab vedotin (CHEP + brentuximab) or using CHP + brentuximab, but CD30 is not a gate for CHOEP itself.

treatmentSetting: primary therapy for previously untreated nodal peripheral T-cell lymphoma

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: previously untreated peripheral T-cell lymphoma (e.g., PTCL-NOS)
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v2.2026, Peripheral T-Cell Lymphomas PTCL-1 (line 87); CHOEP (Cyclophosphamide/Doxorubicin/Vincristine/Etoposide/Prednisone) listed lines 797 and 801 (PTCL-NOS)

provenance.locator: Grounded to the StewardMD R1-approved R-CHOP backbone (kb/protocols/rchop.json): canonical CHOP cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m2 bsa IV on day 1.

drugs.notes: Cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m2 IV on day 1. The CHOEP (CHOP + etoposide) backbone is grounded to the StewardMD R1-approved R-CHOP (kb/protocols/rchop.json), which encodes the canonical CHOP cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m2 bsa on day 1.

drugs.name: vinCRIStine

drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed., Table 10.1, lines 20759 to 20760: vincristine up to 1.4 mg/m2 IV weekly (bolus), maximum 2 mg per dose. CHOEP uses the 1.4 mg/m2 day-1 bolus dose with the 2 mg cap. ISMP tall-man vinCRIStine; capped at 2 mg per dose.

drugs.name: Etoposide

provenance.locator: DERIVED from the T-cell Lymphomas footnote (approximately line 1059): oral etoposide 200 mg/m2 may substitute on days 2 to 3 and PO etoposide dosing is 2x the IV dose, so the IV dose is 200/2 = 100 mg/m2. This is a derivation from the oral-substitution footnote, not a directly-printed IV value.

drugs.notes: Etoposide 100 mg/m2 IV on days 1 to 3. DERIVED (not a directly-printed IV value): Standard Guidelines (NCCN), T-cell Lymphomas v2.2026 footnote (approximately line 1059) states oral etoposide 200 mg/m2 may substitute on days 2 to 3 and that PO etoposide dosing is 2x the IV dose, so the IV dose is 200/2 = 100 mg/m2.

supportiveCare: G-CSF: primary prophylaxis is commonly required (etoposide added to CHOP increases febrile-neutropenia risk).
Tumor lysis syndrome prophylaxis for high tumor burden.
Antiemetics: moderate to high emetic risk; prophylaxis per emetogenicity tier.

cumulative anthracycline dose tracking (warn 450, hard 550 mg/m2)

guideline.locator: Peripheral T-Cell Lymphomas PTCL-1 (line 87); CHOEP (Cyclophosphamide/Doxorubicin/Vincristine/Etoposide/Prednisone) lines 797, 801; CD30 on diagnostic panel lines 346, 352

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for CHOEP in peripheral T-cell lymphoma (#80). Only vincristine is dose-grounded: 1.4 mg/m2 IV on day 1, maximum 2 mg per dose (DeVita Table 10.1, lines 20759 to 20760, upper end of the cited 0.5 to 1.4 mg/m2/wk bolus range). The CHOP backbone is grounded to the StewardMD R1-approved R-CHOP (kb/protocols/rchop.json): cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m2 day 1, doxorubicin 50 mg/m2 day 1 (anthracycline cap warn 450 / hard 550 mg/m2), and the steroid 100 mg flat days 1 to 5 (rchop names it Prednisolone; this file uses Prednisone, the same interchangeable CHOP steroid at 100 mg flat days 1 to 5). Etoposide 100 mg/m2 IV days 1 to 3 is DERIVED (not directly printed) from the Standard Guidelines (NCCN), T-cell Lymphomas v2.2026 footnote (approximately line 1059: oral etoposide 200 mg/m2 is 2x the IV dose, so IV = 100 mg/m2). No dose now remains VERIFY (vincristine 1.4 mg/m2 is grounded to DeVita Table 10.1). Regimen identity is grounded to Standard Guidelines (NCCN), T-cell Lymphomas v2.2026 (PTCL-1 line 87; CHOEP lines 797, 801). CHOEP is CHOP plus etoposide; CD30, on the diagnostic panel, gates brentuximab-containing alternatives, not CHOEP. ISMP tall-man applied (DOXOrubicin, vinCRIStine [2 mg cap]); anthracycline cumulative cap 450/550 mg/m2. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
